subject: Intermittent SNAT asymmetry after MTU change - EdgeCore private cutover
messages:
From: Nate Brooks <nate@edgecore.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packet drops and weird port mapping after MTU change

Hi Soojin / Vanessa,

We completed the scheduled MTU normalization on our colo routers late last night (1500 -> 1400) and are now seeing intermittent failures on large uploads to our S3-backed service sitting behind Redwood Private. Symptoms: long stalls during large POSTs (10s of seconds), TCP retransmit bursts, and in a couple of packet captures we see the return traffic arriving with a different source port mapping than the outbound (i.e., asymmetric SNAT).

I attached a short pcap that demonstrates an upload where the server receives different 5-tuples on return packets. This is happening across ~5% of connections during peak concurrency. No config changes were made to Redwood side that I know of — the only change was the MTU on our side.

Can you escalate? This is impacting a small but critical customer segment.

Attached: tcpdump_snat_fragments.pcap (pcap, 2.1MB)

Thanks,
Nate Brooks
NetOps Lead, EdgeCore Systems

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Nate Brooks <nate@edgecore.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packet drops and weird port mapping after MTU change

Nate — thanks for the heads up and the pcap. I’ve triaged this thread into priority-high and looped in Marcus and Mina from network reliability. Initial hypothesis: MTU reduction caused fragmentation or changed path MTU behavior which interacted poorly with our egress SNAT/encapsulation path (conntrack hashing + possible port remap on failover).

Immediate asks:
- Nate: can you share the route trace (traceroute -T) to our egress IP and the customer-facing gateway IPs while reproducing?
- Can you confirm whether your colo changed any firewall/NGFW that could be doing port translation?

Short-term mitigation options we can action this morning: rollback MTU on your side back to 1500 for a canary window, or we can apply an MSS clamp and tweak conntrack timeouts on our egress gateway. We’ll coordinate whichever you prefer.

I’ll start looking at egress gateway conntrack logs and port allocation patterns.

—
Soojin Lee
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Nate Brooks <nate@edgecore.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packet drops and weird port mapping after MTU change

On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 09:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Nate — thanks for the heads up and the pcap. I’ve triaged this thread into priority-high ...

I pulled the egress gateway conntrack logs for the time window in the pcap. Findings:
- We saw sporadic conntrack collisions when ephemeral port allocation overlapped during high concurrency bursts.
- Several flows showed fragmentation flags set (DF cleared) and segments reassembled by the host, indicating PMTU/MSS mismatch.
- There are a couple of recent minor changes in our encapsulation path (vxlan decap on the on-prem edge) that affect hash input to our SNAT algorithm. That likely changed the distribution of flows across worker processes which surfaced a port reuse edge case.

Attached a config diff and a snippet of conntrack table entries we captured: egress-gw-config-diff.txt

Immediate recommendation: implement MSS clamp at the egress gateway (to 1360) and increase conntrack hash buckets for the vxlan decap worker to reduce collisions. If the customer prefers, we can temporarily revert MTU to 1500 while we deploy the fix.

I’ll coordinate the change window — suggest a 30-minute canary for a single POP followed by broader rollout.

-Marcus
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Nate Brooks <nate@edgecore.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packet drops and weird port mapping after MTU change

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 10:15 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> I pulled the egress gateway conntrack logs for the time window in the pcap. Findings: ...

Action plan (proposed, can execute within the hour):
1) Canary POP: apply MSS clamp 1360 + increase conntrack buckets on our WY-Edge POP (single POP). Monitor for 1 hour.
2) If canary looks good: roll the same to remaining POPs in 15-min staggered windows.
3) If not improved: rollback to 1500 MTU on EdgeCore for a 2-hour window (they agreed to this as a fallback).
4) Postmortem: create NETOPS ticket and document root cause and config changes.

Playbook excerpt attached: mss-clamp-playbook.md (contains CLI commands and rollback steps). Marcus — please include exact sysctl/iptables commands in the playbook before we execute.

I will schedule the canary at 15:30 PDT and monitor TCP metrics (retransmit rate, 5xx responses). Nate — please keep an eye on your side and share traceroutes if you see anything odd during the window.

—
Mina Haddad
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Nate Brooks <nate@edgecore.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packet drops and weird port mapping after MTU change

Thanks all — canary results look good. We saw the retransmit rate drop from ~4.8% to 0.6% on the sampled prefixes after you applied the MSS clamp and increased conntrack buckets on WY-Edge. The asymmetric SNAT instances in the earlier pcap were not observed during the canary window.

Next steps we agreed on call:
- Redwood will roll the MSS clamp change globally in the next maintenance window and push the conntrack buckets increase.
- EdgeCore will hold MTU at 1400 for 24 hours and run extended large-upload tests; if we see any regression we’ll revert MTU on our routers.
- Postmortem: NETOPS-4128 will include root cause analysis showing interaction between vxlan-decap hash inputs and ephemeral port allocation under fragmentation conditions. We will add a design note recommending a coordinated MSS-clamp or end-to-end PMTU confirmation for future MTU cutovers.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

-Nate
NetOps Lead, EdgeCore Systems

--
